key_facts: Grad F presented a revised semantic specification and construction formalism on a single sheet.
The semantic specification includes a designation of head constituents for meaning and form.
There was discussion about renaming "constraints" due to potential bias or misinterpretation.
Semantic bindings were discussed, including the idea of mental spaces and their implications for meaning.
Professor C suggested deferring detailed mental space implementation until Robert returns.
Grad F mentioned challenges with stress and focus in relation to information structure.
Grad A noted that focus is not always determined by stress but can be inferred from context.
Discourse segments include roles like speaker, hearer, and referents, with some uncertainty about how they are resolved.
The group plans to refine constructions for tourist and child language learning domains over the summer.
Inheritance among constructions was acknowledged as a possible future refinement but not prioritized now.
Grad A shared updates regarding JavaBayes integration and ontology-based modeling ideas for construal.
A Bayes-net approach for dynamic construal was proposed, involving instantiating domain ontologies and contextual modules.
Grad A will present a thesis proposal draft shortly before leaving on Thursday.
The group agreed to meet again at 4 PM on Thursday for further discussion.
